issues.description: The UML in problem_statement.md declares numberOfInscribedStudents as int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as long. This mismatch will confuse students about the expected type and can introduce subtle errors when implementing methods that use this attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute type consistent across artifacts. Either change the UML and any method signatures in the problem statement to use long for numberOfInscribedStudents, or change the solution's declaration to int. Ensure all methods that use this field (e.g., total-count computations) use matching types after the change.

issues.description: The solution's getTotalNumberOfStudents() method is declared to return int but sums a long (numberOfInscribedStudents) and an int, which is a long result — this will not compile. The problem UML also specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, so either the attribute or the method return type is inconsistent across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure consistent numeric types: either change numberOfInscribedStudents to int (so getTotalNumberOfStudents can safely return int), or change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long and update any related methods (and the UML) to use long. Update all artifacts (problem statement, template hints, and solution) to reflect the chosen type so students are not blocked by compilation/type errors.
